policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV "Simon Peter therefore also cometh" renders the adverbial καί; the omission leaves "also" unaccounted for.
All three are the same reflexive/pronoun spelled differently; "unto their own home" renders any of them identically.
Case of μνημεῖον after the preposition and the order of ἔξω/κλαίουσα; ASV "standing without at the tomb weeping" carries every element and English order does not fix Greek order.
ASV opens the verse "When she had thus said" with no conjunction, where the ASV elsewhere renders an initial καί (cf. "also" in v. 6).
The variant is only the article before Ἰησοῦς; English "Jesus saith unto her" cannot show a Greek article on a proper name.
Article before Ἰησοῦς only; "Jesus saith unto her" renders both alike.
Μαριάμ and Μαρία are alternate forms of the one name; ASV "Mary" renders either.
ASV "saith unto him in Hebrew" renders Ἑβραϊστί, which the omission lacks.
Article before Ἰησοῦς only; the verse's one note is classed alternative_rendering and concerns "Touch me not", not this unit.
ASV "not yet ascended unto the Father" has no possessive here, in contrast to "unto my Father" later in the verse; the added μου would be rendered "my Father".
Alternate forms of the same name; ASV "Mary Magdalene" renders either.
ἀγγέλλουσα and the compound ἀπαγγέλλουσα are both "telleth"; ASV does not distinguish them.
ASV reports her words as direct speech in the first person, "I have seen the Lord", which is Ἑώρακα; the third-person ἑώρακεν would give "that she had seen".
The added τῶν is only the article in "the first day of the week", which the ASV's definite phrase renders either way.
ASV "where the disciples were" renders no participle; the added συνηγμένοι would give "were gathered together".

The readings differ by a connective καί and by an αὐτοῖς placed before the objects; ASV "And when he had said this, he showed unto them his hands" carries both a connective and "unto them" but its English order cannot say which Greek word or position supplies them, and αὐτοῖς is also available at v017.

ASV has both "unto them" and "his side", and the pronoun for either can come from this slot or from v016; "his" is in any case a natural supply, as with "his hands", which has no Greek pronoun in either reading.
ASV names the speaker, "Jesus therefore said to them again"; the omission leaves the subject unexpressed.
Perfect ἀφέωνται against present ἀφιένται; ASV "they are forgiven unto them" renders either.
Article before Ἰησοῦς only; "when Jesus came" cannot show it. The verse's note is classed other and glosses Didymus.
Word order of μου and τὴν χεῖρα only; ASV "my hand" renders both.
ASV opens "Thomas answered and said unto him" with no conjunction; the added initial Καί would be rendered "And".
ASV "in the presence of the disciples" has no possessive; the added αὐτοῦ would give "his disciples".
Present against aorist subjunctive of πιστεύω; ASV "that ye may believe" renders either aspect.
